flashcards.q: Deutsch-Jozsa: query counts quantum vs classical?
flashcards.a: One quantum query vs 2^(n-1)+1 classical worst case, under the constant-vs-balanced promise. H^n, phase oracle, H^n; P(|0..0>) = |2^-n sum (-1)^f(x)|^2.

flashcards.q: Grover iteration count formula and examples?
flashcards.a: k ~ (pi/4)sqrt(N/M) for M marked of N items. N=16, M=1 -> k=3 (success 0.961); N=10^6 -> k~786; success after k iterations = sin^2((2k+1)theta), sin(theta)=sqrt(M/N).
Bennett-Bernstein-Brassard-Voyer (1997) proved black-box search needs Omega(sqrt(N)) quantum queries; Grover matches the bound. No exponential generic search is possible.

flashcards.q: What happens if you run more than ~sqrt(N)/4*pi Grover iterations?
flashcards.a: Overshoot: the state keeps rotating past the marked axis and success probability falls again; iteration count must match known/estimated M (or use fixed-point/partial-search variants).

flashcards.q: Grover's effect on symmetric crypto key strength?
flashcards.a: Exhaustive search over 2^b keys costs ~2^(b/2) quantum ops: AES-128 -> 2^64 effective, AES-256 -> 2^128. Symmetric crypto is weakened (halved), not broken; answer is bigger keys/hashes.
Factoring N -> order-finding (r of random g mod N) -> period-finding of g^x mod N via QFT + continued fractions -> gcd(g^{r/2} +/- 1, N); >=50% success per trial, repeat ~2x.

flashcards.q: Why Q ~ N^2 in the period register?
flashcards.a: Need Fourier resolution so multiples of Q/r separate beyond aliasing: spacing Q/r > 1 guaranteed when Q > r^2, and r < N always; hence pad to next power of two above N^2.

flashcards.q: Which part of Shor dominates cost?
flashcards.a: Modular exponentiation (reversible arithmetic): O(n) multiplications each with thousands of Toffoli/T equivalents; the QFT itself is cheap O(n^2) gates and semi-classical variants shrink it further.
~20 million noisy physical qubits running ~8 hours, surface code at 10^-3 physical error (2019). Newer arithmetic compilations push toward ~1M+ qubits over days. Credible window: mid-to-late 2030s.

flashcards.q: RSA vs ECC under Shor: which dies cheaper?
flashcards.a: ECC: ECDLP-256 needs far smaller registers (~256-512 qubit width vs ~4096-bit for RSA-2048 arithmetic) and simpler operations, orders of magnitude fewer logical qubits/runtime. Both broken; ECC first as hardware scales.

flashcards.q: Phase kickback definition and role here.
flashcards.a: Ancilla |-> turns controlled-X action into a phase ((-1)^f(x)|x>): eigenvector stays intact while eigenvalue lands on control. Used by DJ/BV to encode f, by Grover's oracle (diagonal sign matrix), and in Shor's readout.

Any routine succeeding with probability p becomes O(1/sqrt(p)) repetitions instead of O(1/p) by reflecting about the input state; gives quadratic Monte Carlo speedups too. Still needs a coherent marking unitary.

flashcards.q: Do quantum computers solve NP-complete problems efficiently?
flashcards.a: No known exponential win; BQP is not believed to contain NP. Generic optimisation gets at most quadratic Grover-style gains plus unproven heuristics; claims otherwise conflate oracle models with worst-case complexity.
